title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #151 review (frontend-channel-overlay)
description: Tracked non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #151 (frontend-channel-overlay), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Distinct from the PR's own blocking finding (the candlestick-occlusion bug), which stays on frontend-channel-overlay itself and must be fixed before that PR can be accepted.

checklist.step: Consider a lightweight visual-regression/screenshot check for the chart panes (PriceChart.tsx/OscillatorChart.tsx). No existing test -- neither the mocked vitest unit tests (which stub addSeries/setData and never render real pixels) nor the persisted Playwright e2e suite (which asserts on DOM/console state, not chart pixel content) -- would have caught the PR #151 review's candlestick-occlusion bug (an opaque AreaSeries painting over real candlestick data). That bug was only found via a manual, one-off browser walkthrough. Worth evaluating whether a cheap screenshot-diff check on a couple of representative fixture tickers/ranges is warranted for this chart-rendering-order class of bug, or whether the cost/flakiness of visual-regression tooling outweighs the benefit here -- a genuine judgment call, not a mandate to add one.

Non-blocking (PR #151 retry-round-1 re-review): PriceChart.tsx's post-fix `series.setSeriesOrder(2)` (the candlestick series' target render index) is a literal magic number, not derived from the actual number of series added before it in the effect. Verified correct today by tracing Lightweight Charts v5.2.1's source (addSeries appends to the pane's data-source list; setSeriesOrder splices/reclamps against that list's length at call time) -- with exactly zoneTopSeries and zoneBottomMaskSeries added before it, index 2 is right. But nothing ties the literal `2` to 'however many series exist at this point in the effect': a future change that adds/removes/reorders a series in this effect before line 411 without also updating this number would silently re-occlude candlesticks (the exact bug this PR fixed), and the existing regression test (PriceChart.test.tsx asserting `setSeriesOrder` was called with `2`) would keep passing since it only checks the literal argument, not the resulting z-order relative to the zone series. Consider deriving the target index at call time instead (e.g. `series.setSeriesOrder(zoneBottomMaskSeries.seriesOrder() + 1)`) so it can't drift out of sync with the series actually added above it.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 2 (the `series.setSeriesOrder(2)` magic-number finding) is already fully resolved on `main`, before this followup task was even picked up -- no new code change needed here, just verification and closing the loop on the board. `frontend-support-resistance-overlay` (PR #152, merged before this task started) replaced the literal `setSeriesOrder(2)` call with a new shared `bringSeriesToFront(chart, series, paneIndex = 0)` helper in `utils/chart.ts`, which computes `chart.panes()[paneIndex].getSeries().length - 1` at call time instead of hardcoding an index -- exactly the fix this checklist item asked for (deriving the target index dynamically rather than trusting a literal tied to 'however many series exist today'). Verified by reading `utils/chart.ts` (`bringSeriesToFront`'s own doc comment explicitly narrates this exact history: 'the original fix's setSeriesOrder(2) only stays correct as long as exactly one effect ever adds fill series to the pane... recomputing the target index... is self-healing regardless of add/run order') and by grepping `PriceChart.tsx`, which now calls `bringSeriesToFront(chart, series)` from every one of its 5 overlay-adding effects (value-zone/channel, Tide-region shading, support/resistance zones, false-breakout markers' own effect, kangaroo-tail marker effect) rather than any hardcoded index anywhere in the file. `PriceChart.test.tsx` also already asserts this dynamically (`setSeriesOrderMock` backed by a live mock `panes()[0].getSeries()` array that mirrors real add/remove calls, asserting the exact sequence of dynamically-computed indices across all effects, not a single literal) -- confirmed by re-running `PriceChart.test.tsx`/`StockCharts.test.tsx` (67/67 passing) and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (clean) on this branch.
decisions.rationale: The magic-number risk this checklist item flagged (a future series added/removed before the candlestick reorder call silently drifting out of sync with a hardcoded literal) is structurally eliminated by `bringSeriesToFront` computing the index from the pane's actual live series count rather than any hardcoded value -- there's no longer a literal to drift. No alternative approach was considered since the existing fix already matches (and slightly generalizes, via the reusable helper + explicit paneIndex parameter) the checklist item's own suggested remedy; re-implementing a different mechanism to 'complete' an already-closed item would be pure churn.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 (whether to add a screenshot-diff/visual-regression check for PriceChart.tsx/OscillatorChart.tsx): decided NOT to add pixel-based visual-regression tooling (e.g. Playwright's `toHaveScreenshot`) for these chart panes.
decisions.rationale: Lightweight Charts renders entirely to `<canvas>`, and canvas output is sensitive to GPU/font-hinting/anti-aliasing/DPI differences across host OS and CI runner versions -- this project has no existing per-OS golden-image baseline infrastructure (Playwright's own screenshot assertions need one, committed and re-generated on legitimate visual changes), and standing that up is a materially bigger, more failure-prone addition than this followup's own 'lightweight' framing calls for; a flaky visual-regression suite that needs frequent manual re-baselining would likely get ignored or disabled, which is worse than not having one. Weighed against that cost, the actual risk this checklist item is about -- the z-order/occlusion bug class -- has since been substantially mitigated by cheaper means that predate this task: (1) `bringSeriesToFront` (see the other decision entry above) turns the exact bug class (a hardcoded, driftable z-order index) into a self-healing computed value, removing the main way this bug previously got reintroduced silently; (2) `PriceChart.test.tsx`'s mocked-but-live `panes()[0].getSeries()` tracking now asserts the *actual resulting z-order* after every effect runs (not just that a literal argument was passed), which is a meaningfully stronger regression net for this specific bug class than it was at PR #151 time; (3) this project's own review pipeline (`pr-reviewer`/`task-qa-reviewer`) already does a mandatory real-browser walkthrough for any change touching chart rendering order, which is exactly how the original occlusion bug was actually caught -- a cheap, human/agent-driven check that doesn't require maintaining OS-specific golden images. Considered and rejected: (a) full-page `toHaveScreenshot` visual-regression via Playwright -- rejected for the flakiness/baseline-maintenance cost above; (b) a narrower canvas-pixel-sampling Playwright check (read specific pixel colors from the chart's canvas via `page.evaluate`/`getImageData` at a coordinate known to correspond to a below-zone candle for a specific fixture ticker/range) -- a real, more targeted middle ground that would avoid most of the cross-platform anti-aliasing flakiness of a full image diff, but still ties a test to Lightweight Charts' internal pixel-coordinate mapping (autoscale margins, canvas DPI scaling) with no stable public API for that mapping, making it fragile to unrelated future changes (a new overlay, an axis-margin tweak) in a way that would produce false failures disconnected from the actual bug being guarded against; judged not worth the added maintenance burden given the mitigations in (1)-(3) above already exist. This is explicitly the kind of cost/benefit call the checklist item itself frames as optional ('a genuine judgment call, not a mandate to add one'), not something the docs pin down one way or the other.

review.notes: Task-closure PR, no production code touched (git diff main...task/frontend-channel-overlay-followups --stat confirms only docs/tasks/frontend-channel-overlay-followups.json and docs/tasks/index.json changed). Independently verified both claims rather than trusting the decision entries at face value: (1) `bringSeriesToFront` in frontend/src/utils/chart.ts (line 88) computes `chart.panes()[paneIndex].getSeries().length - 1` at call time -- a genuinely dynamic index, not a hardcoded literal -- and `git log -S"bringSeriesToFront"` confirms it was introduced in commit 1ee2e33 / PR #152 (frontend-support-resistance-overlay), predating this followup task, corroborating the 'already fixed by prior work' claim. Grepped all of PriceChart.tsx: zero direct `setSeriesOrder(<literal>)` calls remain; all 5 overlay-adding effects (value-zone/channel at line 1055, Tide-region shading, support/resistance zones at 1232, false-breakout markers at 1379/1466, kangaroo-tail markers at 1562) call `bringSeriesToFront(chart, series)` instead, matching the decision entry's inventory exactly when cross-checked against `useEffect` boundaries (911/974/1132/1255/1422/1528). PriceChart.test.tsx's `panes: () => [{ getSeries: () => [...paneSeries] }]` mock is a live, mutating array (not a static stub), so its `setSeriesOrderMock` assertions do exercise the dynamic-index behavior, not just a literal argument. (2) Read the 'decided against visual regression testing' rationale in full: it's a genuine cost/benefit judgment call (no golden-baseline infra + canvas/GPU/font-hinting flakiness vs. the z-order bug class now being structurally mitigated by (a) the self-healing bringSeriesToFront fix, (b) PriceChart.test.tsx's live z-order assertions, (c) the pipeline's mandatory browser walkthrough for chart-rendering changes), considers and rejects two concrete alternatives (full-page screenshot diff; canvas pixel-sampling) with specific reasons for each, and is explicitly framed by the checklist item itself as optional ('a genuine judgment call, not a mandate to add one'). This is a defensible engineering tradeoff, not test-coverage-dodging -- accepted as-is. Ran full suites as sanity checks despite no code changes: backend pytest --cov=app (807 passed, 99.92% coverage), frontend vitest --coverage (616 passed across 62 files, 99.62% statements / 98.86% branches -- both well above the 90% gate, no regression from the prior known-good state), backend ruff+mypy clean, frontend eslint clean, `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` clean, and scripts/validate_tasks.py clean (189 task files, no board-structure violations). No UI surface changed by this PR (no production code touched) -- browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) are both explicitly skipped for that reason, per the 'no UI surface skips this' carve-out. No new non-blocking findings surfaced by this review beyond what the task's own decisions already document, so no additional followup task was created.

Grepped PriceChart.tsx myself: zero literal `setSeriesOrder(N)` calls remain; exactly 5 `bringSeriesToFront(chart, series)` call sites (lines 1055, 1232, 1379, 1466, 1562), matching the review's inventory.
